chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Faraj, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, who said:

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim wrote to him in the year two hundred and thirty-three, asking him about a man who died and left behind a wife, sons, and daughters, and left for them a غلام whom he had endowed for them for ten years; then he would be free after the ten years. He asked: Is it permissible for these heirs to sell this غلام while they are in need, if it is as I have described to you? May Allah make me your ransom.
So he, peace be upon him, wrote: They are not to sell him until the appointed time of his condition, unless they are compelled to do so; then it is permissible for them.

key_terms.أَوْقَفَهُ: designated or endowed him for a specified beneficiaries' use
key_terms.الْوَرَثَةِ: the legal heirs of the deceased
key_terms.حُرٌّ: free, no longer enslaved after the stated term
key_terms.عَشْرَ سِنِينَ: a fixed period of ten years
key_terms.مُضْطَرِّينَ: being under compulsion or pressing necessity
key_terms.مِيقَاتِ شَرْطِهِ: the appointed time set by the contractual condition

ai.seo_question: Can heirs sell an endowed servant before the end of a fixed emancipation term if they are in need?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal question about a غلام designated for the heirs' benefit for ten years and then set to become free. The ruling states that the heirs may not sell him before the term ends, except in a state of genuine necessity, in which case the sale is permissible.
